item.title: Xi, Japarov sign treaty to deepen ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Xi, Japarov sign treaty to deepen ties Leaders pledge to boost Sino-Kyrgyz friendship and mutual support At around 11:30 am local time on Monday in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, President Xi Jinping and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov put their signatures to a treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, after which they exchanged copies of the treaty, shook hands and posed for photographs. The two presidents also signed a joint declaration on the high-quality development of the China-Kyrgyzstan comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, and witnessed the exchange of bilateral cooperation documents covering investment, transportation, customs and sister-city relations. During Xi's visit, which began on Sunday, the two sides signed more than 20 additional cooperation documents in areas including science and technology, education, culture, people-to-people exchanges and the media. While holding bilateral talks with Japarov, Xi said that high-level political mutual trust and firm mutual support are important guarantees for the steady and long-term development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. China firmly supports Kyrgyzstan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and supports the country in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He added that China stands ready to continue firmly supporting Kyrgyzstan on issues concerning each other's core interests. Japarov said he was honored to welcome Xi to Kyrgyzstan on the 35th anniversary of the country's independence, which fell on Monday. The visit further demonstrated the profound friendship and high level of political mutual trust between the two countries and marked an important milestone in bilateral relations, he said. Xi said the signing of the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will provide an important legal foundation for friendship between the two countries from generation to generation and for their continued mutual support. China is advancing the building of a strong country and national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, while Kyrgyzstan is making every effort to implement its National Development Program through 2030, Xi said. China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to better align their development strategies, deepen exchanges of experience in governance and deliver more tangible outcomes through practical cooperation, he said, calling for taking profound and concrete measures in building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. Xi called for the two sides to deepen practical cooperation by implementing their intergovernmental economic and trade cooperation plan, diversifying traded goods and fostering new growth drivers such as digital trade and cross-border e-commerce. He called for the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, describing it as a "major transportation artery" carrying the development aspirations of people across the region. The two sides should also modernize border crossings and strengthen "soft connectivity" in institutions, standards and rules, he said. Xi urged more landmark projects in renewable energy and resource recycling, as well as efforts to implement cooperation documents on green minerals and expand collaboration across entire industrial chains. He also called for facilitating personnel exchanges and expanding cooperation among young people, as well as media, tourism, sports, healthcare and subnational exchanges, to further consolidate public support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship. The two sides should expand law enforcement and security cooperation, jointly combat the "three forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, as well as drug trafficking and transnational crime, and work together to safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi said. China supports Kyrgyzstan in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs and is willing to strengthen coordination with the country within the United Nations framework, he said. Xi called on the two countries to jointly implement the four global initiatives, oppose hegemonism and power politics, uphold true multilateralism, safeguard international fairness and justice, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system. As founding members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, China and Kyrgyzstan should advance the implementation of the outcomes of last year's Tianjin summit, promote common development in the region and take the SCO's development to a new level, said Xi, who is also in Bishkek for this year's SCO summit. Japarov said the signing of the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will open up broader prospects for bilateral relations. "The People's Republic of China is an important priority in Kyrgyzstan's foreign policy, and our main trade and investment partner. China is our good neighbor, close friend and time-tested, reliable partner," Japarov told Xi. Japarov also said that Kyrgyzstan is willing to expand cooperation with China in trade and investment, connectivity, scientific and technological innovation, energy, minerals and the green economy, while strengthening exchanges in education, healthcare, culture and youth affairs. Kyrgyzstan is ready to work with China to combat the "three forces" and safeguard regional security, he said. Japarov also expressed his country's willingness to strengthen coordination with China through multilateral platforms, including the UN, the SCO, the China-Central Asia mechanism and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. During the talks, Japarov, on behalf of the Kyrgyz government and people, extended his deep sympathies over the mudslide disaster in Gyirong county of China's Xizang autonomous region. Xi thanked him and said the Communist Party of China and the Chinese government are making every effort to search for missing Chinese and foreign nationals, relocate affected residents, treat the injured and guard against secondary disasters. China has also sent rescuers to Nepal and provided emergency assistance, he said. Earlier on Monday morning, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrived by car at Yntymak Ordo, the Kyrgyz presidential administration building, under the escort of a Kyrgyz cavalry guard. They were warmly received by Japarov and his wife, Aigul Japarova. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Peng visits Kyrgyz historical museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Peng visits Kyrgyz historical museum China and Kyrgyzstan attach great importance to preserving and passing on traditional culture, Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi Jinping, said on Monday, as she expressed hope that the two nations will continue to expand people-to-people exchanges and further enhance mutual understanding between their two peoples. Peng made the remarks when visiting the National Historical Museum of the Kyrgyz Republic in Bishkek, the capital of the Central Asian country, with Aigul Japarova, wife of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. During the visit, Peng and Japarova watched a welcoming performance together, and then appreciated an exhibition on traditional Kyrgyz culture. The costumes, carpets and other items on display are exquisitely crafted and richly colored, reflecting the Kyrgyz people's long-standing handicraft traditions and unique customs, Peng said. They also visited an art exhibition on ancient Chinese civilization and watched a Kyrgyz ethnic costume show, where they both expressed willingness to promote cultural exchanges and mutual learning between the two countries. The three-month exhibition, titled "Harmony Creates Beauty: An Art Exhibition of Ancient Chinese Civilization", opened on Aug 18 at the National Historical Museum. It features 153 exhibits from China's Tianjin Museum and Inner Mongolia Museum, as well as from the Kyrgyz museum. The National Historical Museum of the Kyrgyz Republic is the highest-level national museum in Kyrgyzstan, housing a collection of artifacts that traces the history and development of the Kyrgyz people. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade' President Xi Jinping expressed on Monday China's readiness to work with Uzbekistan to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and usher in a new "golden decade" for bilateral relations. Xi made the remarks during a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the China-Uzbekistan comprehensive strategic partnership. Xi emphasized the improvement and upgrading of bilateral ties, the fruitful outcomes of bilateral cooperation in various areas, and the achievements in the building of the China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future. He called on the two countries to advance the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, expand cooperation in artificial intelligence and desertification control, and pursue win-win outcomes. As founding members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, China and Uzbekistan should work together to implement the outcomes of last year's Tianjin summit and promote regional development and prosperity, he added. Mirziyoyev said that Uzbekistan is firmly committed to developing relations with China and stands ready to work with China to deepen political mutual trust, expand trade and investment, and promote people-to-people exchanges. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed President Xi Jinping called on China and Mongolia to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and strengthen the bonds between their peoples, during a meeting with Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, on Monday. The two sides should inject greater vitality into their comprehensive strategic partnership and advance the building of a China-Mongolia community with a shared future, Xi said. Peaceful coexistence, mutual support and win-win cooperation have always been the defining features of bilateral relations, Xi said, adding that China will continue to place ties with Mongolia high on the agenda of its neighborhood diplomacy. Xi stressed the need for the two countries to consolidate the political foundation of their relationship, and respect each other's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity. Xi also called on the two sides to strengthen coordination and collaboration in multilateral affairs and jointly address global challenges. Khurelsukh said that deepening friendly cooperation with China is a top priority of Mongolia's foreign policy, while reaffirming his country's firm commitment to the one-China principle. Mongolia is willing to work with China to advance the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, he added.

item.title: Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed Exchanges and cooperation between China and Russia have maintained a dynamic momentum of development, President Xi Jinping said on Monday when meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. In May, Putin made a successful state visit to China. Xi noted that he and Putin had made arrangements from a strategic, long-term perspective to take bilateral relations to a higher quality and a higher level of development. They also reached consensus on deepening cooperation across various fields under new circumstances. Both countries' relevant authorities are actively implementing the consensus and have already achieved many outcomes, Xi said. He expressed confidence that under their strategic guidance and through joint efforts, the foundation of the relationship will become more solid, progress will be steadier, and prospects will be brighter. Putin noted that bilateral cooperation has developed rapidly. Russia is willing to maintain high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade, energy, industry, transportation, and science and technology, and enhance people-to-people exchanges, he said. Speaking on the international situation, Xi said currently changes unseen in a century are accelerating, and uncertainties and unforeseeable factors in the international landscape have markedly increased. However, pursuit of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes by peoples around the world remains unchanged, he said. The SCO shoulders the mission of maintaining regional stability and promoting development, he said. Putin said Russia and China should continuously strengthen unity and cooperation within the SCO and play a leading role.

item.title: More Kyrgyz youths opt for Mandarin tests
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
More Kyrgyz youths opt for Mandarin tests Candidates rush to embrace broader opportunities as bilateral ties flourish The number of people appearing for Mandarin proficiency tests in Kyrgyzstan has surged more than threefold over the past five years, reflecting a growing interest in the Chinese language amid deepening economic ties and educational cooperation between the two countries, the administrator of the HSK examination said. Li Peize, general manager of Chinese Testing International Co, which administers the exam, said the total number of HSK candidates across all levels grew from 3,139 in 2021 to 12,611 in 2025 in Kyrgyzstan. According to Li, in the first half of the year, more than 7,600 candidates took the test, with the annual total expected to exceed 15,000. The number is projected to surpass 20,000 by 2028, making Kyrgyzstan the first Central Asian country to reach that milestone, he said. He said that Kyrgyzstan's interest in China shows that the bilateral relationship has entered a golden era. "Economic and trade needs have created a broad market, policy support has built a solid bridge, and the desire to study in China and cultural identification have injected endless vitality," he added. China has become a major source of investment in Kyrgyzstan. Major projects — from hydropower stations and ski resorts to financial investment zones — have created abundant local job opportunities, Li said. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway and cross-border e-commerce have further fueled demand for professionals with both Chinese-language skills and technical expertise, he added. The Chinese Embassy in Kyrgyzstan has for years run a scholarship program that requires applicants for full scholarships to have completed at least HSK Level 3. Four Confucius Institutes and more than 20 Confucius classrooms have been established in the Central Asian nation, along with a Luban Workshop and a Silk Road School for cross-border e-commerce — initiatives that link language learning with vocational training and employment, he said. Li noted that a growing number of young Kyrgyz people also consider Chinese as a gateway to better opportunities. China's world-class educational resources, increasingly convenient visa policies and transportation links have made studying in China more attractive than ever. The profile of Chinese learners in Kyrgyzstan has also diversified. Test-takers now include university students, civil servants, translators, business professionals and skilled workers — evidence that Chinese is shifting from a cultural interest to a practical tool for career advancement, he added. For many Kyrgyz students, learning Chinese has opened doors to new experiences and opportunities in China. Ayana Bazarkulova, 20, a student at Beijing Foreign Studies University, said that she has been interested in Chinese culture since childhood. After two years in China, she described the country as "highly developed and modern, especially in terms of technology". "Almost everything can be done online — shopping, ordering food and paying bills, by using digital payment systems. It makes daily life very convenient and efficient," she said. Bazarkulova added that Chinese people are "friendly, kind and welcoming" toward international students. Having studied Chinese for nearly three years, she finds the language fascinating. "The Chinese characters are very interesting, each with its own meaning and history. I also like the tones because they make the language different from many others," she said. Erkemai Zarylbekova, 19, a student at Beijing International Studies University, said that her older sister inspired her to learn Chinese. After two years of study, she said China is a modern, safe and convenient country to be in with its excellent public transportation and advanced technology. "Chinese people have always been friendly and helpful to me. Even when my Chinese was not very good, many people were patient and encouraged me," she said. Nuraiym Aibekova, 27, a second-year PhD student at the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing, first came to China in 2018. She returned to campus in 2023 and said China has become "like a second home". She praised the country's safety, cleanliness and convenience — from online shopping to efficient public transportation. She passed HSK Level 4 after only four months of intensive study and later obtained levels 5 and 6. "At first, I learned Chinese because it was necessary for my studies and daily life," she said. "However, as my language skills improved, I realized that Chinese opened many new opportunities for me." zoushuo@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Social media fuels Chinese yoga wear boom
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Amid the global yoga culture boom, Chinese yoga wear brands have expanded overseas and found favor with international consumers. On TikTok, a young girl from the United States shared her thoughts on her recently discovered favorite brand CRZ YOGA — a sportswear brand from Guangzhou, Guangdong province. In front of the camera, she tried on four sets of yoga wear. "The quality is good. The material is super light. I like the texture of the clothes. The color is what I look for. I wear CRZ YOGA to the gym every day," she said. The video received thousands of likes and comments, and many other users also praised the Chinese brand. Ashton and Ryan, a couple from the US, tried on yoga wear together on a video posted on TikTok. "I already went to the gym today, but I feel like going to the gym again," Ashton said. They also favor yoga wear from Halara — another Chinese brand. Relying on a mature flexible supply chain in China, domestic yoga clothing brands have established a high cost-effectiveness advantage. With platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, they are gaining popularity among overseas consumers. On US online shopping giant Amazon, CRZ YOGA performs well, often occupying nearly half of the top 10 spots on the women's yoga pants bestseller list, and often taking the top spot on the women's sports short skirt list. Among its products, the high-waisted nude yoga leggings priced at $26 are the best-selling product under the brand, with over 26,000 user reviews on Amazon alone. Additionally, CRZ YOGA has also expanded its men's clothing line. To enhance visibility and trust, CRZ YOGA has established a matrix of Instagram, TikTok and YouTube accounts in social media marketing, producing content based on the characteristics of different platforms. On TikTok, it collaborates with small — and medium-sized influencers to shoot "one outfit, multiple wear" lifestyle videos, and showcase the versatility of products and achieving significant results. According to data from market researcher Jungle Scout, one of the brand's $32 yoga pants sold more than 80,000 units on TikTok in a month, with a monthly revenue of $2.84 million. Halara, a sportswear company based in Beijing, entered the US market in 2023. It opened several official TikTok accounts, including a main account with 700,000 followers, with content focused on dressing up and interacting with cute pets. Its popular topics have drawn more than 1 billion views. Data from cross-border information platform Crosspie revealed that Halara ranked second in sales in the US sportswear category on TikTok in March 2025 and topped the charts in April. The total sales of its four small stores in the US exceeded $63 million, and its flagship store Halara US has been ranked first in TikTok's sports and outdoor categories for four consecutive months. Influencers account for 58.23 percent of total sales. The independent website has received more than 13 million visits in the past three months, with 84.46 percent of the traffic coming from the US. Gabby Hirata, president of Halara, said that going forward, the company will adjust the marketing style and content on social media, while increasing a new round of brand building. "Our website will be optimized and adjusted based on the brand's tone and user habits. "Also, we will continue to diversify our content creator team and continue to release some guidelines to encourage users to share what they want completely freely," she said. Lin Xianping, executive deputy secretary-general of China Urban Expert Think Tank Committee, and associate professor at Hangzhou City University, said: "The reason behind domestic yoga clothing brands quickly opening up overseas markets is the flexible supply chain in China. Also, scenario-based product positioning meets the real consumption needs overseas, with high cost-effectiveness forming a strong market penetration, and short-video social media model reconstructing the overseas marketing path." According to data from China Sporting Goods Federation, China's export value of sports equipment reached $28.39 billion in 2024, a year-on-year increase of 6.77 percent.

item.title: The SCO at 25: Dialogue over division
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
The SCO at 25: Dialogue over division Share - WeChat
Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization are gathering in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. When the SCO was founded in 2001, its primary mission was addressing regional security challenges. Yet over the past two and a half decades, its agenda spans far beyond security, encompassing economic integration, digital infrastructure, connectivity, and people-to-people exchanges. The SCO's greatest achievement over the past 25 years is not simply its expanding membership. It is the powerful precedent it sets: proving that dialogue and cooperation can prevail over division. In a world increasingly fragmented by geopolitical tensions, the SCO offers a practical model for peaceful coexistence and mutual development.

item.title: Chinese consumption shifts to 'experiencing'
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Chinese consumption moves from 'buying' to 'experiencing' Share - WeChat
The consumption trend among Chinese consumers has shifted from "buying" to "experiencing" this summer — with soccer chants and desert stargazing emerging as the new spending currency in 2026. From 450-million-yuan ($60.93 million) targeted vouchers to visa-free entry and instant departure tax refunds, a converging policy toolkit is injecting sustained momentum into the experience economy.

item.title: 25 Years of the SCO: Building a Shared Future
item.description:

25 Years of the SCO: Building a Shared Future Share - WeChat
President Xi Jinping once said, "The Shanghai Spirit has inspired a strong sense of solidarity which ensures the growth of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization." Twenty-five years on, that spirit continues to guide the organization on the road toward a shared future with deeper cooperation and stronger global governance.
